hypotheses.text: The presence of a progressive peripheral axonal neuropathy or distal symmetric polyneuropathy (axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 / CMT2) is uniquely characteristic of DHX9 pathogenic variants and is absent in classical DHX30- and DDX6-related neurodevelopmental syndromes.
hypotheses.rationale: While intellectual disability and hypotonia overlap heavily across DExD/H-box helicase disorders, peripheral nerve involvement has specifically been documented in heterozygous DHX9 cohorts and linked to distinct nucleolar mislocalization, offering a key clinical discriminator from DHX30 and DDX6.

evidence.text: Calame et al. (2023) identified 20 individuals with heterozygous DHX9 variants where phenotypes ranged from neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) to distal symmetric polyneuropathy axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2), with CMT2-associated variants causing aberrant nucleolar accumulation.

source.title: Monoallelic variation in DHX9, the gene encoding the DExH-box helicase DHX9, underlies neurodevelopment disorders and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: Phenotypes ranged from NDDs to the distal symmetric polyneuropathy axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2).

hypotheses.text: Cardiomyopathy, specifically ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy or cardiac conduction defects, occurs in a specific subset of ATP-binding domain DHX9 missense variants, distinguishing them from the structural congenital heart defects or normal cardiac anatomy typically seen in DHX30 and DDX-related disorders.
hypotheses.rationale: Non-compaction cardiomyopathy is a rare non-neurologic manifestation; Yamada et al. (2023) identified this finding in a DHX9 ATP-binding site variant alongside cardiac conduction abnormalities in an animal model, indicating a potential non-neurologic discriminator for this sub-cohort.

evidence.text: Yamada et al. (2023) reported a patient with a heterozygous de novo missense DHX9 variant (p.Gly414Arg) in the ATP-binding site presenting with intellectual disability, short stature, and ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy, with corresponding Dhx9 mutant mice demonstrating cardiac conduction abnormalities.

source.title: Heterozygous loss-of-function DHX9 variants are associated with neurodevelopmental disorders: Human genetic and experimental evidences
source.quote: Herein, we report a patients with a heterozygous de novo missense variant, p.(Gly414Arg) of DHX9 who presented with a short stature, intellectual disability, and ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy.

hypotheses.text: Sensorineural hearing loss occurs with significant frequency in DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder, providing a discriminative sensory feature that separates it from standard DHX30-related intellectual disability.
hypotheses.rationale: In Dhx9 knockout mouse models, sensorineural hearing loss was specifically demonstrated as a prominent phenotypic deficit, suggesting inner ear or auditory nerve pathology might distinguish DHX9 dysfunction from other helicase encephalopathies.

evidence.text: Calame et al. (2023) demonstrated that Dhx9-/- mice display sensorineural hearing loss alongside tremor and hypoactivity in novel environments.

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic prevalence of peripheral neuropathy (clinical or electrophysiological) among patients with DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder compared to cohorts with DHX30-related disorder?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether subclinical or clinical axonal neuropathy is specific to DHX9 or overlaps with other DExD/H-box helicase conditions provides the strongest non-CNS discriminator for clinical workup.

new_directions.question_text: Does left ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy represent a recurrent feature of DHX9 ATP-binding motif variants or an isolated co-occurrence?
new_directions.rationale: Determining if cardiac surveillance should be routinely recommended for DHX9 patients with ATP-binding site variants will help establish diagnostic and management criteria distinct from DHX30.
